correctness.rationale: For each finite t, conditioning on the last renewal proves Phi_t(X)=S_t E^t(X)+Tr(X)B_t with positive B_t of trace 1-S_t. Direct subtraction gives Y_t=nu_(t+1) sigma + sum_(s=1)^t nu_s S_(t-s)(h_(t+1)-h_(t+1-s)) E^(t+1-s)(sigma), with trace h_(t+1). Increasing h makes Lambda_t(X)=(1-h_(t+1))E(X)+Tr(X)Y_t CPTP and the composition exact. For a drop at index m+1, cyclic shift dimension m+2 isolates the negative site-m coefficient h_1 S_(m-1)(h_(m+1)-h_m); invertibility of Phi_m makes this unique intermediate and rules out even P-divisibility. Exact Fraction example yields -2/25 and checker passes 60 finite-step groups plus 15 exact negative witnesses. No simulation substitutes for the analytical all-time proof.

value.rationale: The parent work presents non-divisibility under age-dependent resets without a protocol-wide boundary. The theorem identifies the exact classical hazard-order condition that guarantees completely positive intermediate channels for every possible underlying quantum CPTP map, constructs their physical replacement components, and shows sharpness by a finite witness at any age of rate decline. This separates reduced CP-divisibility from microscopic renewal memory and has relevance for designing age-dependent, nonexponential quantum reset protocols.
